title: Signal runway dispatch and release slate — April 2026
content:
Purpose:
This is the working dispatch for the April release window: a compact checklist + 7-day rollout slate + draft release notes. Intended for launch conductor, observability, SRE, and product owners. Use this as the single source for on-call signals and immediate rollback criteria.

TL;DR:
- Ship runtime v2.3.1 (serving runtime kernel and batching tweaks) + hosted model alias swap for mix-1.
- Canary plan: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% over ~72 hours with automated hold gates.
- Key signals: p95 latency, tail servfail rate, KV cache hit ratio, memory OOM surge.

Preflight checklist (pre-deploy, owners noted):
- [ ] Release artifacts built and signed (owner: Diego Morales) — verify SHA256 and artifact-store retention 30d.
- [ ] Canaries configured in orchestration (owner: Ava Chen) — confirm route rules and fallback to mix-1-quantized variant.
- [ ] Telemetry dashboards created and pinned (owner: Priya Iyer) — p50/p95/p99 latency, errors/sec, 5xx ratio, CPU/GPU utilization.
- [ ] Load tests for sustained 2x baseline traffic (owner: Lena Thompson) — attach latest run results GH-PR-4821.
- [ ] Safety lanes: rate-limiters and circuit breakers set (owner: Samir Gupta) — thresholds copied to Slack #deploy-alerts.
- [ ] Backfill/rollback binary in staging validated (owner: Diego Morales) — smoke test script smoke/deploy-smoke.sh passes.
- [ ] Customer impact spreadsheet updated (owner: Product PM) — list customers on Dedicated pools that require scheduled maintenance.

Canary rollout cadence (target timeline):
Day 0: Preflight window (08:00–12:00 UTC) — final signoff by release conductor (Ava).
- 12:30 UTC: Push artifacts to staging and run smoke suite (5m).
- 13:00 UTC: Initiate canary 1%

Day 1: Canary expansion (UTC times approximate)
- 00:00: Monitor overnight signals; auto-hold if p95 > 1.5x baseline for 30m or 5xx > 0.5% sustained 10m.
- 08:00: Expand to 5% if green.
- 16:00: Expand to 20% if green.

Day 2: Validation and majority traffic
- 08:00: Expand to 50% if green.
- 20:00: Full rollout to 100% if green OR hold for manual review (conductor decision).

Hold gates and automatic abort conditions:
- Abort and roll back if any of the following occur for a sustained period (see signal spec below):
  - p95 latency > 1.8x baseline for 15 minutes.
  - Error rate (5xx) > 0.5% sustained 10 minutes.
  - Queue depth on GPUs > 2500 requests for > 5 minutes (risk of cascading timeout).
  - KV cache hit ratio drops by > 20% from baseline for > 10 minutes.
  - Any new OOMs on serving nodes.

Signal spec (how we will measure and where):
- p50/p95/p99 latency: telemetry/dashboard "svc/serving/runtime/latency" — sliding 5m window. Baseline measured during last 7 days.
- Error rate: "svc/serving/runtime/errors" tagging by status_code. 4xx are allowed for bad inputs; 5xx triggers hold.
- KV cache hit ratio: "svc/serving/cache/hit_ratio" — watch for sudden drops after rollout.
- GPU memory pressure: "infra/gpu/mem/percent_used" — alerts at 92%+
- Throttles: "svc/routing/throttled_reqs" — unexpected throttles imply backpressure.

Rollforward / rollback playbook (quick steps):
- Immediate rollback command: orchestration rollback --target previous-stable --force. (owner on-call SRE).
- If rollback: run postmortem triage checklist and collect heap dumps + KV cache dump.
- If small failure (non-critical): open incident, pause rollout, revert canary traffic to last green percentage, escalate to kernel team.

24-hour conductor checklist (what to check every shift):
- Hourly: confirm no hold gates triggered, quick glance at p95 and 5xx.
- 4-hourly: check GPU queue/latency heatmap and top 5 stack traces in error logs.
- Shift handoff: create one-line summary in #deploy-digest channel and update this doc.

Quick smoke tests (post-deploy verification):
- Synthetic call: generate 256-token completion to mix-1 model for canonical prompt set (owner: QA).
- End-to-end critical path: user auth -> route lookup -> inference -> response 200 (owner: Solutions Eng).
- Embedding sanity: compute embeddings for sample payloads and compare cosine to baseline (owner: Research Applied ML).

Draft release notes (to be refined for customer-facing copy):
Title: Serving runtime v2.3.1 and model routing improvements (April 2026)
What changed:
- Upgraded serving runtime with improved continuous batching heuristics and a kernel-level micro-optimization that reduces small-sequence token latencies by ~18% in internal tests.
- Adjusted routing policy to prefer mix-1-quantized for low-latency paths when capacity constrained.
- Fixes for intermittent KV cache invalidation that caused increased cold-starts for short-lived sessions.

Why it matters:
- Expected p95 latency improvement for short-sequence workloads (conversational assistants, chat completions).
- More predictable unit cost under bursty traffic due to better batching.

Behavioral changes for customers:
- No action required for hosted API users.
- Dedicated customers who pinned older runtime versions will not automatically migrate; contact support to schedule.

Known issues (preliminary):
- Rare discrepancy in embedding vector order for a small subset of legacy prompts — patch in v2.3.2 scheduled.
- Observed higher KV invalidation rate in one Dedicated customer's cluster during load test (investigating).

Post-release follow-ups (owners):
- Kernel perf regression sweep (owner: Diego Morales) — due 2026-04-20.
- Eval-run against our saved prompt sets to detect quality regressions (owner: Research Applied ML, Priya Iyer) — due 2026-04-18.
- Customer outreach to top-10 customers on Dedicated (owner: Customer Success) — coordinate calendar invites.

Open questions / risks to resolve before finalizing:
- Should we widen the initial canary to 2% instead of 1% to speed validation? (ops impact vs. safety) — input requested from SRE.
- Does the hosted API SLA window require an additional standby pager for the first 24 hours? (legal/ops)

Notes to conductor (informal):
- Keep an eye on batch-size distribution; if mean batch size drops by > 30% it could expose a regression in batching heuristics.
- If we see spike in user-level 429s, check routing throttle rules before blaming models.

Appendix: quick commands and links
- Rollout command (kctl): kctl apply -f deploy/v2.3.1/canary.yaml
- Rollback command: kctl rollout undo deployment/serving-runtime --to-revision=stable
- Smoke script: tools/smoke/deploy-smoke.sh — use --parallel 5 for perf mode.
- Dashboards: https://telemetry.internal/redwood/deploy-v2-3-1
- Slack channels: #deploy-alerts, #serving-runtime, #cs-updates
- Jira: JIRA-RELEASE-2214 (release epic), JIRA-4578 (kernel micro-opt)

Revision history:
- 2026-04-10 (Ava Chen): initial draft and cadence proposal.
- 2026-04-12 (Priya Iyer): added signal thresholds and linked telemetry dashboards.

If anything ambiguous — ping me (Ava) directly. This doc is intentionally compact; expand sections you own and mark status when ready.
